learning_from.description: The learner's explanation/best language. Every canonical learn-from language may participate when its localized bridge and reusable fact copy exist.

learning_language_full.description: Tier 1 and Tier 2 target languages with researched family-member distinctions, representative terms, cultural cautions, examples, and practice-ready relation features.

learning_language_game.description: All 104 canonical learn-from languages have the same 14 broad family relationship concepts in the universal game vocabulary package. Slash-separated forms preserve lexical subdivisions instead of being flattened into one fake equivalent.

learning_language_comparison.description: Every canonical language may participate as a comparison/game target. Tier 3 does not imply a full grammar or culture curriculum path; rich language-and-usage profiles remain Tier 1 and Tier 2 until separately researched.

runtime_model.source_first: Show the localized source bridge in the learner's best available language before teaching the target system.
runtime_model.target_second_full: For Tier 1 and Tier 2, resolve the structured target profile and render its relationship distinctions and cultural-usage cautions through reusable support-language fact templates.
runtime_model.target_second_tier3: For Tier 3, expose the 14-concept universal term set to comparison and Games. Do not synthesize a rich cultural profile from the vocabulary row.
runtime_model.pair_scaling: Never author a source-by-target matrix. Source copy, reusable localized facts, target profiles, and universal game terms are independent assets joined through stable relationship concepts.
runtime_model.fallback: If a support-language localization is below the user's trust threshold, use the normal best-language fallback. If a target lacks a rich profile, use the Tier 3 comparison/game path rather than inventing target prose.
